analysis:
This PR changes only operator-facing CLI text for served-request counters. DoctorRunner.swift lines 223 and 241 reword the doctor messages. StatusCommand.swift line 174 now calls the new Status.servedRequestLines (StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift lines 10-24). The tests in DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift are updated to match.

The new helper reads only DaemonState.stats (requestsServed, tokensGenerated, cancellationsPartialComplete) and uptimeSeconds. These are already-local daemon state fields that the old code printed. It adds no new data source, network call, file write, key material, prompt content, or authorization logic. The output shows aggregate counts and static explanatory text, so it exposes no consumer prompts (A-001), keys (A-003), or attestation/authorization evidence (A-015, A-016).

The text states that the counts are not paid-job records and points operators to the console Earnings page. That is more accurate and does not weaken T-053, T-054 or T-052. It does not feed into serving authorization, trust levels, or routing decisions.

One unverified item: StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift calls compactDuration unqualified, while StatusCommand.swift uses Self.compactDuration. The helper and compactDuration are both static members of Status, so it resolves. This is a compile-correctness question, not a security one. The stats.cancellationsPartialComplete optional is presumed to exist in ProviderCore.DaemonState and was not visible in this batch.

No regressions against the retained threat model were identified, and no threat-model update is needed.
